source.title: Feature Drift: How Fine-Tuning Repurposes Representations in LLMs
source.authors: Andrey V. Galichin; Anton Korznikov; Alexey Dontsov; Oleg Y. Rogov; Elena Tutubalina; I. Oseledets

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal-direction interventions using directions reconstructed from SAE features selected by harmful-versus-harmless activation differences, rather than directly applying only the original difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal outcomes for ablation and addition of reconstructed SAE directions, plus an ablation comparison with the true refusal direction. SAE transfer FVU, feature-drift ER/IR, and direction reconstruction NMSE/cosine results are not refusal-behavior outcomes. The study does not report results for V2–V8.
record.test_reason: The study re-runs Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means refusal-direction ablation on Gemma-2-2B-IT as a reference (r5): all layers and positions, JailbreakBench, HarmBench classifier. Its main rows (r1–r4) intervene with SAE-reconstructed directions (cos ≤0.51 to the true direction). Those are the study's own method, not the difference-in-means direction V1 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that instruction tuning repurposes existing base-model features (feature drift) rather than creating new ones. Base-SAE features that drift to activate on harmful instructions in the chat model mediate refusal: ablation drops safety from 1.0 to ∼0.1, and addition induces refusal about half the time. Base-selected features fail at both.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means to select SAE features separately in base and chat models, then non-negative least squares over their decoder vectors to reconstruct the direction. It applies ablation across all layers and token positions, but addition at the middle layer.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention outcomes differ according to whether the reconstructed features are selected from chat-model or base-model activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Directions rebuilt from the top-64 chat-model SAE features (cos 0.51 to the true direction) cut the safety score from 1.0 to ∼0.1 when ablated. Added at the middle layer, they induce refusal on ∼50% of benign prompts. Base-model-feature reconstructions (cos 0.34) only reach a safety score of ∼0.7 and induce <5% refusals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse features that come to activate on harmful instructions after instruction tuning can partly reconstruct the refusal direction and causally control refusal; features selected in the base model cannot.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Findings of EACL 2026)
record.problems: The causal refusal case study uses one model family and size (Gemma-2-2B-IT). Outcomes are reported approximately, with no uncertainty estimates. Safety is scored by an automated classifier and benign refusal by a substring heuristic. The study does not test whether other capabilities remain intact.
record.rows_left_out: No additional refusal-behavior results were left out. Table 1 reconstruction NMSE/cosine values and Sections 3–4 and Figure 3 transfer and feature-drift metrics were excluded because they do not report refusal behavior under intervention.

untested.parts: Preservation of other abilities after ablation or addition is not measured. Only one model (Gemma-2-2B-IT) is tested. True-direction addition is not reported in the text (figure only).
Harmfulness judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
No transfer of the direction across languages or models. Base SAE features are tested, but not the transfer of a base-model direction.

missing.what: Refusal score on benign Alpaca prompts when adding the true difference-in-means direction at layer 15. It is plotted in gray in Figure 2 but has no row and no numeric value in the text.
Un-intervened baselines: safety score on JailbreakBench and refusal score on Alpaca for Gemma-2-2B-IT with no intervention.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the SAE-reconstruction rows to V1. V1 concerns the difference-in-means direction itself, so only r5 (the true-direction reference) bears on it, and r5 is a figure-only replication on one 2B model. Limits of the evidence: no uncertainty is reported, benign refusal is scored by a substring classifier, and no capability check is run. The partial addition effect (r2) belongs to the reconstruction, not the true direction, so it is not a limits_scope verdict on V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether general capabilities remain intact. Addition is tested at the middle layer, not across every layer; it reports an approximate refusal rate rather than refusal on all harmless prompts.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not compare affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Does not test transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct models.
Does not vary how or when refusal is trained.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the reconstructed direction formed from the top-k chat SAE features across all layers and token positions during generation.
rows.note: The paper says the score falls from 1.0 to approximately 0.1 at k=64, matching the true refusal direction’s effectiveness.
rows.check: Ablates an SAE-decoder reconstruction (cos 0.51 to the true direction), not the difference-in-means direction V1 names. This is the study's own method, so the finding goes under fits_no_version. The baseline of 1.0 is the score at small k, not an un-intervened control.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Added the reconstructed direction from top-k chat SAE features at the middle layer across token positions.
rows.note: Addition induces refusals on about half of the benign prompts, not all of them.
rows.check: Adds the reconstructed SAE direction, not the difference-in-means direction; this is the study's own method. The un-intervened refusal rate on Alpaca is not stated.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the reconstructed direction formed from the top-k base SAE features across all layers and token positions during generation.
rows.note: The authors describe base-feature reconstructions as failing to bypass refusal effectively; the score only reaches approximately 0.7 at k=64.
rows.check: Base-SAE reconstruction (cos 0.34) is the study's own comparator, not the V1 direction. It bears on the feature-drift hypothesis, not on any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Added the reconstructed direction formed from the top-k base SAE features at the middle layer across token positions.
rows.note: The paper says base-feature reconstructions fail to induce refusals.
rows.check: Base-SAE reconstruction addition is the study's own comparator, not the V1 direction.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the true difference-in-means refusal direction across all layers and token positions during generation.

conditions.value: true refusal direction, harmful-minus-benign difference in means

rows.note: The text says the chat-feature ablation at k=64 matches the true refusal direction’s effectiveness; it does not give a separate numerical value for the true-direction condition.
rows.check: Value is figure-only. The text says chat ablation at k=64 (∼0.1) matches the true direction's effectiveness, implying a safety score of roughly 0.1 for the true direction. The un-ablated baseline is not stated numerically.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-2B-IT, true difference-in-means direction ablated at all layers and positions, 100 JailbreakBench prompts, HarmBench classifier
relationships.reason: The text says chat-reconstruction ablation to ∼0.1 safety score matches the true direction's effectiveness, so true-direction ablation removes most refusal (r5). The value is read from text and figure only.
relationships.display_finding: True-direction ablation matched chat-reconstruction ablation's effectiveness at a safety score of approximately 0.1, indicating substantial refusal removal.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: Ablation reduced the safety score from 1.0 to approximately 0.1, consistent with removal of most refusal behavior (r1, r5).
